title: Dhammapada Verses
credit: Pāḷi text and English translation as in Mor’s Pāḷi Workshop booklet.

paras.en:
One may live a hundred years
with no paññā and no samādhi.
Better it is a single day of life
for one who has paññā and meditates.

One may live a hundred years
without seeing arising and passing away.
Better it is a single day of life
for one seeing arising and passing away.

One who does not take anything as “mine”,
throughout this mind and body,
who does not sorrow over that which is not —
he is truly called a bhikkhu.

Whenever one comprehends
the arising and passing away of the aggregates,
one experiences rapture and joy,
for the discerning, that [leads to] the Deathless.

“And what, bhikkhus, are the five clinging-aggregates that, in brief, are dukkha? They are:
the material form clinging-aggregate,
the vedanā clinging-aggregate, the perception
clinging-aggregate, the saṅkhāras clinging-aggregate,
and the consciousness clinging-aggregate.
These are the five clinging-aggregates that,
in brief, are dukkha.
This is called the noble truth of dukkha.”
